messages:
Elena Ruiz: quick note from today's all-hands q&a thread 1: collecting the process items people asked about so leadership can respond in one place.

Tom Becker: couple of practical ones: 1) will release rhythm change for product teams or infra too? 2) whats the expected QA/bench coverage for infra runtime patches?

Nia Johnson: summary from leadership: product teams default to a two-week sprint + release, with weekly canaries optional for urgent/fast-moving features. infra/runtime teams should keep a tighter loop (weekly) for low-risk patches, or stage rollouts for risky changes.

Nia Johnson: QA/bench expectations: every runtime or infra PR touching hot paths needs a minimal perf bench and a smoke deploy plan. aim to measure at least: p95 latency, alloc_per_req, and qps under typical load. regressions > 10% need mitigation.

Sanjay Rao: oncall clarification: rotation stays weekly for primary; secondary is 2 weeks. we'll trial a single shared slack handoff post on Monday 09:30 PT to reduce confusion. more in eng-sre.

Elena Ruiz: product question came up in the live q&a about SLAs 1: what latency numbers do we publish for Dedicated vs Hosted and are fallbacks automatic?

Maya Patel: for customer-facing guidance: Hosted API public guidance is "best-effort" latency with p95 targets listed per model in the catalog. Dedicated customers have contractual p95 latency targets (examples: small seq p95 <= 200ms, long-context up to 600ms depending on model). yes, automated fallback chains exist (model_family -> region -> degraded-capacity model) and are enabled by default for critical routes. we'll add clearer FAQ text.

Tom Becker: can we get a small PR template snippet that enforces perf bench links? a few PRs skipped that and surprised QA.

Nia Johnson: draft checklist below, please comment: 
```
PR checklist (add to template):
- unit tests updated
- bench run attached (link to artifact)
- perf diff: p95, p99, memory, qps (regressions >10% block)
- deployment/canary plan included
- rollback steps noted
- security/data review if applicable
```

CI-Bot: perf checks required by policy for PRs touching /runtime or /serving are queued. see https://redwood.example/ci/policies for details.

Sanjay Rao: i'll publish the standard bench job names and the exact metric ids (latency_p95, latency_p99, memory_bytes_alloc) to eng-sre by EOD tomorrow so teams can script automation.

Elena Ruiz: thanks. also leadership asked for examples of when a product team should choose weekly canaries vs biweekly release 1: will host a 30-min follow-up tomorrow 10am PT to run through example scenarios and the PR checklist. agenda: release patterns, perf gates, oncall handoff, SLA customer messaging.

Maya Patel: i'll coordinate with legal/product to draft the one-paragraph SLA FAQ and share with this thread for feedback.

Tom Becker: will bring a sample bench run link and a small script to attach to PRs.

Elena Ruiz: ephemeral note 1: please keep replies short in this thread so we can paste into the follow-up doc. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
